sections.h2: Hickory Home Prices and Market Pace
sections.html:
In the 24 months from November 15, 2024 to November 14, 2026, 122 residential sales closed in Hickory (Chesapeake, VA) according to REIN MLS records. The median sold price was $717,500, well above the citywide median of $420,000, and homes took a median of 24 days to sell, slower than the citywide median of 18 days. These figures come from closed sales, which show what homes actually sold for rather than asking prices.

The middle half of Hickory sales closed between $550,625 and $893,750, or about $256 per square foot against $219 citywide. Split by year, the median sold price in the most recent 12 months ($750,000, 67 sales) was about 6% higher than in the earlier 12 months ($704,550, 55 sales). The typical home sold right at its list price (median sale-to-list ratio of 100%).

sections.h2: What Kinds of Homes Sell in Hickory
sections.html:
All of the sales were detached single-family homes. The median home was about 2,800 square feet, with the middle half of sales running from roughly 2,113 to 3,374 square feet. 51% of the homes that sold had 4 bedrooms.

Home ages vary widely here: about 80% of sales were built between 1954 and 2021, with a median year built of 1998.

Averages hide a lot, so Chris Jenkins compares you to homes that match yours on street, size, age and condition rather than to the whole Hickory median.

sections.h2: Buying in Hickory With Chris Jenkins
sections.html: If you are buying in Hickory, Chris Jenkins sets up a search for the exact streets and price range you want, pulls the recent sales so you know what a fair offer looks like, and negotiates for you. Because home ages here range from older to brand new, inspect each home on its own: newer homes may carry builder warranties, while older ones may need roof, HVAC or system updates. Because Virginia sellers give a disclosure statement that tells buyers to do their own due diligence, read our guide to the Virginia Residential Property Disclosure Statement. Confirm flood-zone status and insurance cost for any specific home, since these vary lot by lot.

Figures come from closed residential sales recorded in REIN MLS for Chesapeake between November 15, 2024 and November 14, 2026, grouped under the subdivision name MLS agents use. Medians, not averages, are used so a few very high or low sales do not distort the picture. With 122 sales, this is a solid sample, but every home differs and these figures are not an appraisal or a prediction. Subdivision names in MLS data can cover more than one section of a community.
